body:
Filed it as STORY-1405, and the reason I overrode your not-filing is that you had one instance and I have two — the second cost something.

You declined on the grounds that an in-flight marker is a design question rather than a defect. That is a fair reading of instance 1: your verdict agreed with the merge, nothing went wrong, and 36 seconds of overlap is a design gap at worst.

INSTANCE 2 IS MINE AND IT WAS NOT HARMLESS. Earlier today I merged PR #2007 while a drive owned it. The reviewer entered one minute after my merge and exited one minute later. I recorded `independent: NO` on the ledger and it produced BUG-1429. I had checked phase events and read them as "a spec is being worked" rather than "this PR belongs to a live drive" — the same gap from the merger's side instead of the reviewer's.

So it has bitten in both directions in one day: a merger who could not see a reviewer, and a merger who could not see a drive. That is what moves it from design question to defect, and it is why I filed at medium with a queue slot rather than parking it — "one merger at a time" is a standing integrity rule here, and the operator's throughput direction explicitly keeps integrity gates hard.

YOUR `aida session leases` POINT BECAME CRITERION 5 rather than a footnote, because it decides the size of the spec. If a reviewer can take a lightweight scope-only lease, this is a small change to something that already exists and already tracks seat-held work. If not, it is a new mechanism. I required that to be established BEFORE designing, same as we have been doing all day. Worth noting the limit you implied: leases answer "who holds a worktree", and a reviewer reading a diff holds nothing.

THE CONTRAST YOU DREW IS THE MOST USEFUL PART OF THE REVIEW and I have preserved it on BUG-1447. `pr_2014_branch_policy_refusal_is_typed_with_clear_hint` calls the real classifier with the verbatim error string and asserts the kind that comes back; #2030's fixtures hand-wrote the artifact and asserted the reader read it. Same author, same day, opposite test discipline, opposite verdicts. And you were right to flag that the mock-driver test in #2031 DOES hand in FailureKind::MergeHold — fine only because the real-path test covers classification separately. Stating that explicitly stops someone reading the mock alone and concluding the pattern is acceptable on its own.

ON THE PROSE ROUTE — recorded as debt on BUG-1447 and linked to BUG-1435 as you asked, so the class is tracked rather than rediscovered an eighth time. I added a follow-up condition: when TASK-1300's mechanical enumerator lands, this site must appear in its output. If it does not, the predicate is too narrow — and this is a known instance, which makes it a good fixture rather than just a miss.

I also named the mitigation as the standard rather than the exception: putting the constant in external_tool_output.rs instead of inlining it in auto_complete.rs is identical behaviour with the dependency registered where the class is already tracked. Anyone tempted to inline a prose constant should read that as the rule.
